title: rk unified projection graph document (v1)
description: Read-only, deterministic, stateless projection of one rk research campaign (PRD C5, IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md M2.1). The registry (argument/**/*.md shards) is the spine (`nodes`); the other three stores — af, bd, fr — and the generated report join to it by DIFFERENT keys per edge (`edges.af` / `edges.bd` / `edges.fr` / `edges.report`) — there is no universal join key, do not invent one. `unresolved` is a first-class bucket every edge kind's failed lookups land in (never a silent drop). `conflicts` is a first-class defect record, CLOSED to five settled kinds (registry-vs-af disagreement, contract mismatch, taint-vs-status inconsistency, fr banked-without-oracle, and — at v2, rk-0ehr / P1 — retraction-vs-status) as of the Tier A review repair wave (2026-07-19) plus the v2 bump — src/graph/validate.ts RECOMPUTES these from the raw node/edge data and treats a missing/duplicate/inconsistent recorded conflict as an ERROR. See docs/memos/2026-07-19-graph-schema-v1.md for the design rationale (including the review's four landing-blocker repairs) and src/graph/{types,serialize,validate}.ts for the TS mirror + canonical serializer + structural validator (this JSON Schema alone cannot express cross-array cardinality — e.g. 'exactly one af edge per af!=none node' — referential integrity, unresolved-bucket exact accounting, conflict recomputation, or canonical sort order — those are src/graph/validate.ts's job).

schema_version.description: Consumers must check this before parsing the rest of the document; a version bump accompanies any incompatible shape change (CLAUDE.md rule 10), with a fixture. Mirrors the convention set by ../vibefeld's `af export --graph json` (docs/export-graph-v1.md). BUMPED "2" -> "3" by rk-8805: `registryNode` gained `signature`, the Layer 1 signature block (schemas/signature.v1.json) the projection now carries so a consumer can read a result's declared regime without re-parsing shards. A v2 consumer reading a v3 document sees NO signature on any node -- which is precisely the "applied outside its regime" blindness Gate 2 Check 17 exists to remove -- hence a bump rather than a tolerated widening. src/graph/schema-version.ts's `acceptGraphDocument` reads BOTH versions (a v2 document is upgraded in memory with every signature ABSENT, never a fabricated empty one) and refuses anything else; fixtures `corpus/graph/signature-legacy-v2` and `corpus/graph/signature-v3`. PREVIOUSLY BUMPED "1" -> "2" by rk-0ehr / P1 (retraction as a first-class event, docs/memos/2026-08-03-rk-improvement-plan-from-aism.md §P1): `edges` gained a fifth array (`retraction`), the CLOSED `conflictKind` enum gained `retraction-vs-status`, and both `conflictRecord.edge` and the unresolved bucket's `edge` gained `"retraction"`. A v1 consumer reading a v2 document would silently miss every retraction — exactly the failure this schema change exists to prevent — hence a version bump rather than a tolerated widening. The FILE NAME is deliberately unchanged: `$id`/filename track the schema FAMILY, the const above tracks the version (ratified as the standing convention by docs/reviews/2026-08-03-p1p2-validity-wave-tierA-fable.md, ruling 1).

nodes.description: The registry spine, one entry per argument/**/*.md shard. MUST be sorted by `id` ascending in the canonical form (src/graph/serialize.ts) — this is part of the document's identity, not a rendering nicety.

edges.description: The per-edge joins (PRD C5's four, plus `retraction` added at v2). Each array's canonical sort order is defined in src/graph/serialize.ts, not here.

af.description: registry↔af: contract byte-match, LOCATED VIA the shard's `workspace:` field (never the registry id — workspace directories can be renamed independently of the registry id; see ../vibefeld/docs/export-graph-v1.md's `workspace.id` note), targeting ONLY the af export's ROOT node (id "1" — af's hierarchical numbering roots there unconditionally), never a descendant lemma and never `workspace.conjecture`. Every registry node with `af != "none"` MUST have EXACTLY ONE entry here (a cross-array cardinality rule src/graph/validate.ts enforces — this JSON Schema cannot express it). Known hazards: workspace dir ≠ id after a rename (legal) — keyed on `workspace:`, always; contract matching against a non-root node (guarded by the `afRootNodeId` const below).

bd.description: registry↔bd: registry id IS the bd issue key (linker-synced issues). No known hazard.

fr.description: registry↔fr: `evidence.artifact` path resolution + `graduates`/oracle ids. Known hazard: free-text paths — expect a real unresolved-reference bucket, never silently dropped; two distinct unresolved cycles may legitimately name the identical artifact text, so completeness is keyed on `(edge, sourceCycle, ref)`, never `(edge, ref)` alone.

report.description: registry↔report: shard label/id anchors (as check-provenance.py's own anchor resolution does today). Known hazard: anchors are ids, not contracts.

retraction.description: registry↔retraction (v2, rk-0ehr / P1): the campaign's own `.rk/retractions.jsonl` ledger (schemas/retraction.v1.json), joined on `itemId` == registry `id` — the same key bd uses, and the ONLY edge whose source ledger rk writes itself, so there is no foreign-vocabulary hazard here. EVERY record becomes an entry, resolved or not (the fr precedent, not the bd one): a retraction naming an unknown id is a real fact about the ledger, so it stays visible here AND carries a companion `unresolved` bucket entry keyed on `(edge:"retraction", ref)` with EXACT count matching (two records naming the same unknown id are two rows, never one). src/graph/validate.ts enforces referential integrity in both directions — a `resolved:true` entry must name a real node, and a `resolved:false` entry must NOT.

unresolved.description: The first-class unresolved-reference bucket (PRD C5): every edge kind's failed lookups land here. af/bd/report are keyed on `(edge, nodeId)` (an edge names exactly one node); fr is keyed on `(edge, sourceCycle, ref)` (`sourceCycle` is REQUIRED for `edge:"fr"` — see `unresolvedRefFr` below) so two distinct unresolved cycles naming the same artifact text stay two distinct rows, never collapsed into one. A consumer must be able to answer "what did rk try to join and fail" from this array alone, without re-deriving it from the edge arrays' resolution flags.

conflicts.description: First-class defect records — registry-status vs af-epistemic-state disagreement, contract byte-mismatch, taint vs status inconsistency, fr banked-claim without a fresh oracle verdict, and a live retraction standing against an item (v2). CLOSED to these five kinds (Tier A review, memo question 1: a new conflict class needs a schema_version bump, not silent vocabulary extension — typo tolerance is the wrong tradeoff on a validity surface). src/graph/validate.ts recomputes the conflict set the raw data implies and ERRORs on a missing, duplicate, or inconsistent recorded entry. Conflicts are rendered, never auto-resolved.

afEpistemicState.description: af's own epistemic_state axis (../vibefeld/docs/export-graph-v1.md). CLOSED enum (Tier A review blocker 1/3) — an unrecognized value is a validity-surface bug, not tolerated free text.

afTaintState.description: af's own taint_state axis (../vibefeld/docs/export-graph-v1.md). CLOSED enum, same rationale as afEpistemicState.

balloonCounter.description: Reserved (PRD C9 / M3.6 balloon feedback loop): present and zero-valued from M2.1 on, populated only once M3.6 lands.

path.description: repo-relative path to this shard's own file. Never a join key itself — `id` and `workspace` are.

workspace.description: THE join key into af. Raw `workspace:` frontmatter value, e.g. "proofs/lem-x". Absent iff the shard never declared one. NEVER assumed equal to `id` — see edges.af's description and the rename-hazard note above.

deps.description: AND-edges: registry ids. Semantically a SET — canonical order is sorted, not insertion order.

routes.description: OR-groups: each inner array is one route (AND); the outer array is the disjunction (any one route suffices). `[]` when the shard declares no routes.

defs.description: Layer-0 definitions/*.md ids this node cites.

nodeSignature.description: v3 (rk-8805): the shard's Layer 1 signature — what the result REQUIRES of its context (`pre`), what it PROVIDES (`post`), and the ambient predicates it holds under (`regime`). The AUTHORED form is a fenced ```signature block in the shard body (schemas/signature.v1.json, which is normative for the grammar, the closed vocabulary, and the failure codes); this is that block in its PARSED shape, where each pre/post entry's predicate keys sit under `keys` instead of beside `obj`. ABSENT iff the shard declared no signature, or declared one Gate 2 Check 17 refused to parse — a malformed block is a gate ERROR, never graph data. Absent is NEVER rendered as an empty signature: "declared nothing" and "declared the empty regime" are different claims. Canonical form (sorted keys, sorted entries) is part of the document's identity, enforced by src/graph/validate.ts's canonical-form check via src/gates/signature.ts's ONE canonicaliser.

schema_version.description: schemas/signature.v1.json's own version, NOT this document's.

profile.description: The convention profile the vocabulary is drawn from, e.g. "qpcp.v1".

regime.description: AMBIENT (object-free) predicates. They live in their own scope and never satisfy an object-scoped predicate — that conflation is the unsoundness the 2026-08-20 Tier A review (LB2) broke the v1 check with.

nodeSignaturePredicate.description: A predicate on ONE Layer 0 object, in parsed form. `obj` is a `definitions/*.md` id — objects are compared by ID, never by name, which is what makes bite's canonical identity immune to renaming (src/graph/bite.ts).

afEdge.description: A discriminated union on `workspaceResolved` (Tier A review blocker 1: 'unresolved workspace requires a bucket entry; resolved workspace requires af schema version, root-node identity, contract-match verdict, enumerated epistemic/taint states, and node count' — a partial 'resolved' record cannot validate against either branch below).

workspace.description: Copied from the owning node's own `workspace:` field — MUST be byte-identical to it (src/graph/validate.ts enforces this cross-check; a drift means a producer re-derived the join key from `id` instead of copying the field, the exact rename-hazard bug class).

workspaceResolved.description: No af export was found for `workspace` at all. MUST carry a companion entry in the top-level `unresolved` array (edge:"af", nodeId, ref:workspace) — never a silent drop (PRD C5).

workspace.description: Copied from the owning node's own `workspace:` field — MUST be byte-identical to it (src/graph/validate.ts enforces this cross-check).

workspaceResolved.description: An af export WAS found for `workspace`.

afSchemaVersion.description: The af export document's own schema_version (../vibefeld/docs/export-graph-v1.md), echoed for traceability — NOT this document's schema_version.

afRootNodeId.description: MUST be the literal string "1" — af's hierarchical numbering roots there unconditionally (../vibefeld/docs/export-graph-v1.md: dotted ids `1`/`1.2`/`1.2.3`..., only `1` ever has no parent_id). Its presence at this exact value is the mechanical proof the contract byte-match targeted the export's ACTUAL root, never an internal lemma and never `workspace.conjecture` (Tier A review blocker 2).

contractMatch.description: Byte-match verdict between the registry `contract` and the root node's `statement`. MANDATORY once resolved — 'resolved storage, mismatched contract' is a real state (contractMatch:false), requiring a mandatory `contract-mismatch` conflict record, never an unresolved-bucket item.

nodeCount.description: af export's validation.total_nodes for this workspace.

frEdge.description: A discriminated union on `resolutionMethod` (Tier A review blocker 4): `resolvedNodeId` is FORBIDDEN when unresolved and REQUIRED otherwise.

artifact.description: The free-text `evidence.artifact` value from fr's LogRecord — the known hazard (free-text paths).

outcome.description: fr's own outcome for this cycle (open vocabulary, mirrors ../knowledge-frontier's Outcome) — needed to compute the banked-without-oracle conflict class.

verdict.description: fr's own evidence.verdict for this cycle (mirrors ../knowledge-frontier's Verdictish: claimed | audited | banked).

verdictFresh.description: Whether `verdict` is still fresh (non-stale) at projection time.

supersedes.description: cycle of a prior fr record this one supersedes (mirrors LogRecord.supersedes; raw, no supersededBy mirror).

frEdgeUnresolved.description: Keyed by fr's own `cycle` (fr's log.jsonl identity), NOT by registry id. No candidate registry node resolved for this cycle's artifact at all.

frEdgeResolved.description: Keyed by fr's own `cycle`. A candidate registry node WAS resolved for this cycle's artifact.

anchor.description: The report label/id anchor — an id, not a contract.

unresolvedRef.description: A discriminated union on `edge` (Tier A review blocker 4): `edge:"fr"` REQUIRES `sourceCycle`; the other three edges never carry it.

ref.description: The free-text artifact string that failed to resolve.

nodeId.description: The registry node this unresolved lookup was attempted FROM, when known.

sourceCycle.description: fr's own cycle number — REQUIRED: two distinct unresolved cycles may name the identical artifact text, so this field is what keeps them two distinct bucket entries.

ref.description: The raw reference text that failed to resolve — a workspace path (af), a registry id (bd), an anchor (report), or a retraction record's `itemId` (retraction, v2).

nodeId.description: The registry node this unresolved lookup was attempted FROM.

retractionEdge.description: One record of `.rk/retractions.jsonl` (schemas/retraction.v1.json) projected onto the registry. A retraction is an out-of-band demotion of an item whose artifact bytes are UNCHANGED — the one validity event every edit-triggered staleness rule in rk structurally cannot see. THE INCIDENT (CLAUDE.md L2): AISM 2026-07-28, two proofs validated the previous day were found defective by an independent sweep and retracted in prose only, and still read validated in three of four layers (docs/memos/2026-08-03-aism-postmortem/03-datamodel.md, 'Drift & inconsistency found' item 1).

nodeId.description: The record's `itemId`: a registry node id when `resolved`, a dangling reference otherwise.

ordinal.description: The record's position in the append-only ledger — its identity there, and what breaks ties when one item carries several records (highest ordinal wins, in BOTH the conflict computation and the taint trace, so the two can never disagree about which retraction is operative).

contentHash.description: The item's content hash AT RETRACTION TIME, in `hashDomain`.

hashDomain.description: Which of schemas/verdict.v1.json's two PINNED hash domains `contentHash` lives in. The two are NEVER compared to each other. A live `l5-shard-bytes` retraction demotes L5 promotion (docs/gate-contracts.md Gate 2 Check 14); a live `af-canonical` retraction removes the item from the monotone-trust available set (Check 8).

retractedBy.description: Who issued it (e.g. "TJO", "audit:2026-07-28-independent-sweep"). Non-blank is structural, not cosmetic: an unattributed retraction is not auditable.

reason.description: Why. Carried onto the conflict record so a reader sees the withdrawal AND its stated grounds, never one without the other.

resolved.description: Whether `nodeId` names a node in this document. An unresolved entry additionally carries an `unresolved` bucket row — never a silent drop.

live.description: Whether the retraction still BINDS: the item's current hash in `hashDomain` equals `contentHash`, OR that current hash could not be observed at all (fail closed — see `currentHashObserved`). Resolved by the store reader (src/store/retraction-load.ts), exactly as `frEdge.verdictFresh` is; the pure graph layer never hashes a file. Editing the artifact changes the hash and releases the binding, at which point ordinary staleness semantics take over — nothing is lost, because every verdict bound to the old bytes is stale too. A live retraction on a resolved node ALWAYS produces a `retraction-vs-status` conflict, and is a taint SOURCE that cascades over the requirement closure.

currentHashObserved.description: Whether the reader ACTUALLY observed a current hash in this record's domain. `false` means `live` is a fail-closed default, not a confirmed comparison. KNOWN LIMITATION, recorded rather than hidden: rk cannot presently read an item's current `af-canonical` hash (`af export --graph json` carries no node content hash through src/store/af-load.ts), so every `af-canonical` retraction stands until it can. Reversing that default would silently un-retract a claim on the strength of data rk does not have.

conflictKind.description: CLOSED as of the Tier A review (memo question 1). A new conflict class requires a schema_version bump — which is exactly what `retraction-vs-status` got (v1 -> v2, rk-0ehr / P1): a LIVE retraction on a resolved node ALWAYS produces one, unconditionally, whatever the node's declared status is. That unconditional rule is the mechanism by which no render surface can present a retracted item as validated/proved (src/render/styling.ts's `effectivePresentation` folds any conflict naming a node into the defect tier); a veto gated on a status list would silently stop working the day the list drifted. Identity is `(kind, edge, nodeId)`, so several live retractions on one node coalesce into ONE node-level conflict naming the highest-ordinal record.
